meta.scope_statement: Assess helpdesk-mcp before expanding it from the platform-team pilot to company-wide use.

executive_summary.posture: helpdesk-mcp is a first-party remote server fronting the corporate ticketing system, expanding from a pilot to company-wide rollout. It declares Enterprise-Managed Authorization to satisfy the planned centralized-access requirement, but its Authorization Server accepts any validly-signed ID-JAG regardless of audience, so a token minted for any other application in the same IdP tenant is accepted here too. That is worse than not declaring EMA at all: it creates the appearance of centralized enterprise control while remaining bypassable.

findings.title: Enterprise-Managed Authorization declared but ID-JAG audience is never validated
findings.description: The server declares io.modelcontextprotocol/enterprise-managed-authorization in its initialize response, so a connecting client's administrator will treat it as governed by centralized IdP policy. Its token-validation function verifies the ID-JAG's signature against the IdP's JWKS and checks expiration, but never checks the aud claim against this server's own resource identifier.
findings.impact: Any validly-signed ID-JAG issued by the same IdP tenant for a different application is accepted here. An attacker, or a compromised, unrelated internal app, that can obtain any ID-JAG from this IdP gains a valid access token to the ticketing system, entirely bypassing the per-server policy the IdP admin believes they configured. This is a confused-deputy, audience-confusion bypass of the exact control EMA exists to provide.
findings.likelihood: Moderate to high: any other EMA-aware application in the same enterprise IdP tenant is a viable source of a wrong-audience ID-JAG; no privileged access is required to obtain one, only a connection to any other org-approved MCP server or app under the same IdP.

evidence.detail:
def validate_id_jag(token: str) -> dict:
    header = jwt.get_unverified_header(token)
    key = jwks_client.get_signing_key(header["kid"])
    claims = jwt.decode(token, key.key, algorithms=["RS256"])
    # no audience=... kwarg: PyJWT does not check aud unless told to
    return claims

remediation.summary: Pass audience="helpdesk-mcp" (this server's canonical resource identifier) to jwt.decode, and reject any ID-JAG whose aud does not match. Add a test that presents a validly-signed, wrong-audience token and asserts rejection before re-enabling the EMA declaration.

findings.title: Excess OAuth scope requested across a mixed read/write toolset
findings.description: The server requests the tickets.admin scope for the entire tool surface, but only helpdesk_create_ticket and helpdesk_close_ticket need write access; the other three tools are read-only.
findings.impact: Any compromise of the server's token, or a confused-deputy call routed through it, carries admin-level ticketing scope rather than the narrow write scope the toolset actually needs.

remediation.summary: Split into tickets.read (the three read tools) and tickets.write (helpdesk_create_ticket, helpdesk_close_ticket); drop tickets.admin entirely.

profile.purpose: Expose the corporate ticketing system (create, search, and close helpdesk tickets) to agents company-wide.
profile.maintenance_signals: Active internal repo, weekly releases, 3 maintainers.

capabilities.name: helpdesk_search_tickets
capabilities.function: Search tickets by status, requester, or text.

capabilities.name: helpdesk_get_ticket
capabilities.function: Fetch a single ticket by id.

capabilities.name: helpdesk_list_queues
capabilities.function: List ticket queues the caller can see.

capabilities.name: helpdesk_create_ticket
capabilities.function: Open a new ticket in a queue.

capabilities.name: helpdesk_close_ticket
capabilities.function: Close a ticket with a resolution note.

permissions: tickets.admin (requested for the full toolset; helpdesk_create_ticket and helpdesk_close_ticket need write, see F-02)

install_methods: Internal service catalog entry; clients connect to https://mcp.helpdesk.acme.internal
hosting.data_residency: Company-owned infrastructure, same region as the ticketing system.

protocols.forward_compat_notes: No session-derived security decisions observed; compatible with the stateless 2026-07-28 direction.

authentication_and_credential_risk.auth_downstream: Service identity with enforced per-user context (AUTH-5) against the ticketing API.
authentication_and_credential_risk.notes: OAuth 2.1/PKCE and per-user downstream context are sound. The critical gap is entirely in ID-JAG audience validation (F-01).

composition.analysis: Ticket content is internal, and the server has no external-communication tool; the trifecta's third leg (an exfiltration channel) is not present as reviewed.
composition.blast_radius: Full read/write/admin ticketing access for any caller presenting a wrong-audience ID-JAG from the same IdP tenant, company-wide once past pilot.

recommendations.action: Fix ID-JAG audience validation before any expansion beyond the pilot: pass this server's resource identifier as the required audience and reject mismatches, then re-verify with a forged wrong-audience token.
Split the requested OAuth scope into tickets.read and tickets.write; drop tickets.admin.

limitations.disclaimer: Point-in-time assessment (2026-07-21) against the reviewed commit. Static/code review only; the Authorization Server was not exercised live with a forged token in this pass. This report is not a warranty.
limitations.verification_note: F-01 is reasoned (static/definition review): the missing audience check is visible in source, not confirmed by presenting a live forged token. Run the skill-security-review validator, or a live authorization-attack pass, to upgrade to confirmed.
